questions.passage:
Books are our best companions. They enrich our minds with knowledge and open the doors of imagination. Reading good books helps in developing our personality, improving our language, and broadening our outlook. Unlike friends, books never demand anything from us. They are always ready to share their wisdom and experience.
In this modern age of technology, many people have turned away from books to television and mobile phones. Although, these gadgets provide entertainment and information, they cannot replace the joy and depth of reading. Books have the power to transport us to different worlds, teach us valuable lessons and inspire us to achieve greatness.
Every student should cultivate the habit of reading daily. Even a few pages a day can make a big difference in one's thoughts and behaviour. Reading good literature shapes our character and helps us understand life better.

questions.text: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions given below it :
questions.passage:
The ultimate challenge is to make your mind calm and the ultimate solution is meditation. In today's age every second person recommends meditation to the first! And for a student, there cannot be a more powerful technique to improve long term performance in studies and other activities.
Calm mind, better retention, better health, focus and concentration are the obvious benefits. You will realise the benefits, as your practice includes a general sense of well being and happiness and spiritual growth. The mood problem can be taken care of by this way 'meditation'.
There are many types of meditation. The simplest is of course, focussing on breathing. Since your breath is always with you, it can be done anytime, any place. But the best is to settle down in a cool place that has dim light and is relatively quiet. You must focus all your attention on your breathing. Observe your breath as it comes in and goes out. You will see that your mind will tend to wander a lot, but soon you will be able to bring it back on breathing.
Don't obstruct thoughts, let them go off. All you need to do is to keep your focus on breathing. When you try this initially, you will see how difficult it is to do! But soon, you will gain mastery over it and who knows you might end up as a spiritual Guru !

questions.text: Write a paragraph in about 120 words on any ONE of the following topics:

parts.statement: My ideal Teacher
parts.explanation:
MY IDEAL TEACHER

A teacher plays a pivotal role in shaping the character and intellect of students. My ideal teacher is Mr. Sharma, who teaches us English. He possesses profound mastery over his subject and makes complex literary texts and grammar rules simple and interesting. Beyond academics, what sets him apart is his calm demeanor, patience, and empathetic nature. He treats every student with equal dignity, never discouraging those who struggle, but instead motivating them to excel. He instills strong moral values, discipline, and self-belief in us, leading by personal example. Mr. Sharma is not merely an educator, but a true mentor, guide, and philosopher whom I admire and strive to emulate.

parts.statement: Importance of computer in modern age.
parts.explanation:
IMPORTANCE OF COMPUTER IN MODERN AGE

In the modern era, computers have become an indispensable part of human life. From banking, administration, and scientific research to education and entertainment, virtually every sector relies heavily on computers. They execute complex calculations at lightning speed, store vast amounts of data securely, and facilitate instant global communication via the internet. In schools and universities, computers have revolutionized the learning process through interactive visual aids, virtual classrooms, and digital libraries. During crises, they enabled work-from-home models and remote schooling. Without computers, modern transport, space research, and healthcare diagnostics would come to a standstill. Thus, computer literacy has become an essential life skill in the contemporary digital age.

parts.statement: Clean India, Green India.
parts.explanation:
CLEAN INDIA, GREEN INDIA

'Clean India, Green India' is a vital national mission that emphasizes the inseparable relationship between environmental sanitation and sustainable living. Cleanliness is not only essential for personal hygiene and public health, but it also elevates national pride. By eradicating open defecation, managing waste responsibly, and curbing single-use plastics, we can prevent lethal diseases and keep our surroundings pristine. Simultaneously, creating a 'Green India' requires aggressive tree plantation, conservation of natural water bodies, and reducing industrial pollution. Trees act as natural lungs, purifying the air and fighting global warming. Every citizen, particularly the youth, must take active responsibility by adopting eco-friendly habits to transform this vision into reality.

parts.statement: Role of Youth in Nation Development
parts.explanation:
ROLE OF YOUTH IN NATION DEVELOPMENT

The youth represent the most dynamic, energetic, and productive segment of any country's population. They are the backbone of national progress and social transformation. With their innovative ideas, technical expertise, and boundless enthusiasm, young citizens can drive economic growth through entrepreneurship, research, and digital technology. Moreover, youth play a critical role in eradicating social evils such as caste discrimination, corruption, and gender inequality. By actively participating in democratic processes, community service, and environmental preservation, they steer the nation toward inclusive development. To channel this immense potential effectively, society must provide the youth with quality education, vocational skills, and moral grounding.

ANNUAL SPORTS DAY CELEBRATION AT GHSS BHOPAL

By Student Reporter

Bhopal, 18th November 2025:
Govt. Higher Secondary School, Bhopal celebrated its Annual Sports Day with immense fervor on 17th November 2025 at the school sports ground from 9:00 AM onwards. The District Sports Officer graced the occasion as the Chief Guest.

The programme commenced with a ceremonial march-past by the four student houses, followed by the unfurling of the sports flag and the torch-lighting ceremony. Various athletic events including 100m and 200m sprints, 4x100m relay, long jump, shot put, and tug-of-war were conducted amidst enthusiastic cheering from the stands.

The Chief Guest then gave away medals and trophies to the victors, with Tagore House lifting the overall championship trophy. In his inspiring address, the Chief Guest underscored the significance of sportsmanship, discipline, and physical fitness in a student's life. The memorable event concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by the Physical Education Teacher, followed by the National Anthem.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct option: (Any Five)

parts.statement: He {BLANK} football since morning.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) has been playing

Explanation:
The prepositional time phrase 'since morning' denotes an action that started in the past and is still ongoing, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ('has been playing').

parts.statement: She works hard {BLANK} she may get good marks.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (D) so that

Explanation:
'So that' is a subordinating conjunction of purpose, regularly followed by a clause expressing purpose with the modal auxiliary 'may'.

parts.statement: It {BLANK} rain today.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (B) may

Explanation:
The modal auxiliary 'may' is used to indicate possibility or likelihood, such as predicting weather.

parts.statement: {BLANK} Ganga is a holy River.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) The

Explanation:
The definite article 'The' is mandatory before the names of sacred rivers, oceans, and mountain ranges.

parts.statement: The principal is {BLANK} the office.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (A) in

Explanation:
The preposition 'in' indicates a static state or position inside an enclosed space, whereas 'into' indicates movement toward the inside.

parts.statement: Sohan is superior {BLANK} Mohan.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) to

Explanation:
Latin comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' (superior, inferior, senior, junior) are followed by the preposition 'to', never 'than'.

parts.statement: The {BLANK} class was making noise.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: (C) whole

Explanation:
When preceded by the definite article 'the', the determiner 'whole' is used with a singular collective noun (i.e., 'The whole class'). Note that 'all' precedes the article (e.g., 'all the class').

parts.statement: As soon as the students saw the teacher, they became silent. (Rewrite the sentence using 'No sooner.........than')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: No sooner did the students see the teacher than they became silent.

Explanation:
'As soon as' in past tense is rewritten with 'No sooner did + subject + base verb...than' (or 'No sooner had + subject + V3...than').

parts.statement: He shut the window. (Change into negative sentence)
parts.explanation:
Negative Sentence: He did not shut the window.

Explanation:
Since 'shut' is used in the simple past tense (third person singular without '-s'), its negative form is constructed using 'did not + shut'.

parts.statement: I know him. (Change the voice)
parts.explanation:
Passive Voice: He is known to me.

Explanation:
In the simple present tense, the passive takes 'is + known', and the verb 'know' takes the preposition 'to' instead of 'by'.

parts.statement: If they do not work hard, they will not get good marks. (Rewrite the sentence replacing 'If' with 'Unless')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: Unless they work hard, they will not get good marks.

Explanation:
'Unless' means 'if not', so replacing 'If they do not work hard' with 'Unless they work hard' retains the original conditional meaning.

parts.statement: They found a ladder. It was dragged from its place. (Combine the sentence to form a complex sentence with relative clause)
parts.explanation:
Combined Complex Sentence: They found a ladder which was dragged from its place. (or 'that was dragged from its place.')

Explanation:
The relative pronoun 'which' or 'that' replaces the pronoun 'It' to link the subordinate relative clause to 'ladder'.

parts.statement: Urmila is very strong. She can do everything. (Combine the sentence into simple sentence using 'too ... to')
parts.explanation:
Combined Simple Sentence: Urmila is not too weak to do everything. (or: Urmila is too strong not to do everything.)

Explanation:
Because 'too...to' inherently bears a negative restrictive connotation ('so...that cannot'), combining two positive capabilities requires balancing the negation.

parts.statement: The manager will go to Mumbai on Monday. (Change the sentence into past Simple Tense)
parts.explanation:
Past Simple Sentence: The manager went to Mumbai on Monday.

Explanation:
In simple past tense, the future auxiliary 'will go' is replaced with the second form of the verb, 'went'.

parts.explanation: M. Hamel praised French as the most beautiful, clearest, and most logical language in the world. He passionately urged the students and villagers to guard their language among themselves and never forget it. parts.explanation: The ironmaster realized his mistake the next morning in the manor house. However, in broad daylight, after the peddler was cleanly shaved, bathed, and dressed in the ironmaster's fine clothes, the ironmaster instantly recognized that the man was an absolute stranger and threatened to call the sheriff.

parts.statement: What was Gandhiji's politics intertwined with?
parts.explanation: Gandhiji's politics was intertwined with the practical, day-to-day problems of the millions of poor peasants and citizens. His was not a loyalty to abstractions or high theories, but a direct loyalty to living human beings. While fighting the Champaran sharecroppers' case, he simultaneously addressed their sanitary conditions, health concerns, and lack of primary education, demonstrating that political freedom was inseparable from social uplift and human dignity.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 75 words (Any One) (Flamingo)

parts.statement: Write the central idea of the poem 'A Thing of Beauty'.
parts.explanation: The central idea of John Keats's poem 'A Thing of Beauty' is that beauty is eternal and a perennial source of joy. Its loveliness increases with time and never fades into nothingness. Amidst human despondence, suffering, sadness, and dearth of noble nature, shapes of natural beauty—like the sun, moon, old and young trees, clear rills, and daffodils—lift the dark pall from our spirits, giving us hope and reason to love life.

parts.statement: Summarise the poem 'A Roadside Stand'.
parts.explanation: In 'A Roadside Stand', Robert Frost presents the poignant plight of underprivileged rural folks who run a modest fruit and vegetable shed by the highway. They plead for city dwellers to stop their speeding cars and purchase their farm produce to earn some cash. However, affluent city motorists either ignore them completely or criticize their crude signs. Frost condemns the false promises of politicians and 'greedy good-doers' who exploit these innocent rural people while failing to deliver genuine economic relief.

The toy had been carved by an unskilled carpenter, leaving sharp splinters of wood protruding from its surface. While playing, a tiny sliver pierced the Maharaja's right hand. Infection developed rapidly, turning into a suppurating sore that spread throughout his arm. Despite surgery by three famous surgeons, the king died, fulfilling the astrologer's prediction that the hundredth tiger would take his life.
